body:
**Working entry (chk-svgnifag):** Select list and selection debts — highlighted-row contrast shared with a multiple's
chosen row, larger font, highlight's reading, single `size`, Cells' selected cell; founder's forks (v040-04).

**Capability:** `matrix#v040-04` — each of the five debts reaches the founder as a fork; each one fixed is proven
headless on the stand or a fixture in both layout modes, and each one kept stands as a residual with his reason.

**Intent anchor:** escher-0.4.0 intent §Findings 4 ("Every debt of 0.1.0–0.3.0"): each residual comes to the founder as
a fork at its phase — fixed, or kept as a residual by his word with its reason. `drag` (finding 8) owns the select
thumb (`res-ammkrycp`), which is NOT this chunk's.

The five debts, each one a founder fork first, then — for each the founder rules fixed — the fix, proven headless in
both layout modes; for each ruled kept, the residual re-stated with his reason.

1. **Highlighted-row contrast** (`res-tym5wois`) — an open select list's highlighted row's text/background contrast is
   unread by the visual lint (`lint`'s `contrast` defect); today only `select_popup_painted` measures the plain pair
   and the highlight. The working entry ties it to a `multiple` select's chosen row, whose contrast is likewise
   unread. [inferred: that a `multiple` select's chosen row is painted with the same highlight colours and is equally
   unread by the lint]

2. **A larger authored font** (`res-2iu7qn2e`) — the list's row height is the select's font on one line; a larger
   authored font clips in it. [inferred: the clip is in the row's height computation in
   `packages/blitz-dom/src/node/select_list.rs` and/or the painter `packages/blitz-paint/src/render/select_list.rs`]

3. **The highlight's reading** (`res-caouqg3t`) — the highlighted row is in no snapshot and no accessibility tree, so
   an agent pressing keys sees it only in a shot and an assistive technology hears the list open and not which row.
   Any reading added crosses the driver's carriers (snapshot, diff, MCP, kept check) — a closed-value field inside a
   ratified carrier is no widening by the founder's 2026-10-10 rule, a new key or open value still is.

4. **A single select's `size`** (`res-ysz67imk`) — `size` is read on a `multiple` select alone (the founder's F8 at
   2026-10-31-select-popup); a single select with `size` > 1 renders as a closed dropdown instead of a list box.

5. **Cells' selected cell** (`res-wvatzhpe`) — Cells' data cells read author keys `cell-{A..Z}{0..25}` and the edit
   input `cell-input`, but no cell states a selected reading and no grid role is stated (the flight booker and CRUD
   state selected by attribute).

- Every fix that changes engine behaviour reaches every document, remote pages included — an engine change for every
  document, and where a reading leaves on a carrier, possibly a boundary widening: each is the founder's fork.
- The select thumb's drag is out (`res-ammkrycp`, v040-12's «Select list thumb dragged»).
- No new carrier, verb, exit, cause, session error, log field or span is planned; one only by the founder's word.

- The founder answers through the operator, by relay, not in this window. All founder forks are written into ONE
  file, `founder-forks.md` in the run dir — each fork with its measurement, every option with its cost, the
  recommended option first, and the forks' dependencies — and the phase stops there until the relay returns.
  Technical forks that turn nothing of what the product is are the operator's, asked by dialog. [inferred: the
  operator's directive at this take-up, snapped below]

1. **Highlighted-row contrast** (`res-tym5wois`, F1 A) — the visual lint's `contrast` reads an open list's highlighted
   row as painted: the engine's highlight pair (`SelectListView::HIGHLIGHT_TEXT` on `HIGHLIGHT_BACKGROUND`) through the
   harness's one contrast formula, never the row's plain computed pair; and a check pins those two constants equal to

   2026-10-31-select-popup); a single select with `size` > 1 renders as a closed dropdown instead of a list box.

5. **Cells' selected cell** (`res-wvatzhpe`) — Cells' data cells read author keys `cell-{A..Z}{0..25}` and the edit
   input `cell-input`, but no cell states a selected reading and no grid role is stated (the flight booker and CRUD

body:
Question (P4, by dialog): F1 (lint reads the highlighted row as painted): escher-driver cannot name the harness's colour type (`color::AlphaColor`) — its only colour path is `Harness::text_contrast`, which reads computed styles. Where should the painted-pair reading live?

Answer: "New harness reader (Recommended)" — Add a read-only `Harness::highlight_contrast(element) -> Option<TextContrast>` in blitz-test-harness: for the highlighted row of an open list it answers the painted pair (SelectListView constants) with the row's own text size, else None. The lint asks it first, then `text_contrast`. One formula, no new dependency, `text_contrast`'s 'computed styles only' contract unchanged.

changes the stand alone. No carrier, verb, argument, exit, cause, session error, log field or span is added
(security-plan · decision/boundary-widening-rule, decision/closed-value-field-no-widening).

1. **F1 — the harness reader.** In `packages/blitz-test-harness/src/contrast.rs`, add a public read-only
   `Harness::highlight_contrast(element) -> Option<TextContrast>`. It answers only for an element that is the
   highlighted row of the open list, read through `BaseDocument::select_list_view()` (a row whose `node` is the
   element and whose `highlighted` is true). Its `text` and `background` are `SelectListView::HIGHLIGHT_TEXT` and
   `HIGHLIGHT_BACKGROUND` as opaque colours, its ratio from the module's one `contrast_ratio`. Its size fields
   (what `is_large_text` reads) come from the row's own computed font, as `text_contrast` takes them. Any other
   element answers `None`. Like `text_contrast`, it changes nothing: no mutation, pump, settle or time move
   (test-plan · decision/contrast-reader-reads-only), and it prints and logs nothing. Its `///` doc states that it
   reads painted engine constants, not computed styles, and that `text_contrast`'s contract is unchanged.

2. **F1 — the lint.** In `packages/escher-driver/src/lint.rs` `contrast()` (`:537-554`), keep the exemption and the
   text test. Read `harness.highlight_contrast(element)` first and `harness.text_contrast(element)` only where it
   answers `None`. The reason keeps its shape: `ratio` and `required` from the reading, numbers only
   (a11y-plan · contract/lint-contrast-finding/*). The finding, its order and its written form are unchanged.

3. **F2 — the row height.** In `packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs` `measure_select_list` (`:974-1005`), the row
   height becomes the largest `layout.height()` among the rows' own layouts (the loop that already lays out every row's
   label for the width; a header's at weight 700 as `text_row_layout` gives it), divided by the scale, plus
   `2.0 * ROW_PADDING_Y`. The select's own one-line height (`:985`) stays as the floor: a row is never shorter than
   today. `SelectList.row_height` stays one value, so `Geometry`, `place`, hits, scrolling and the thumb are unchanged.
   Update the doc comment's «the select's own font on one line».

4. **F3 — the tree.** In `packages/blitz-dom/src/accessibility.rs`, in the single-select arm (`:241-242`), when the
   list stands open and its `current` is `Some(option)`, call `builder.set_active_descendant` with that option's
   tree id. Nothing is read from a page's `aria-activedescendant`: the existing pin
   `accessibility_active_descendant_unread` stays green unchanged (a11y-plan · decision/active-descendant-unread). Tree
   focus stays on the select (a11y-plan · decision/focus-stays-on-select-with-list-open). Cite HTML-AAM's select and
   WAI-ARIA's `aria-activedescendant` above the call (architecture S4).

5. **F3 — a highlight move marks the set.** In `packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs` `move_select_list_current`
   (`:1048-1054`), insert the open list's select into `changed_nodes` when the highlight actually moves. In
   `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs` `hover_list_row` (`:591-605`), do the same where it moves `current`.
   A wheel move inside the list still marks nothing.

6. **F3 — the snapshot model.** In `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot.rs`, add `NodeState.highlighted: bool`
   after `clickable`, documented. The builder collects every tree node's `active_descendant()` into a set. A node is
   `highlighted` when its tree id is in that set: read from the tree, never the element (a11y-plan ·
   decision/snapshot-reads-the-tree).
   In `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot_text.rs`, write the bare token ` highlighted` after ` clickable`, only
   when true; update the doc's token order. In `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot_diff.rs`, add
   `Reading::Highlighted` before `Bounds`, so `Reading::ALL` has thirteen variants, and compare it in the readings
   table.

7. **F3 — the driver's schema and written form.**
   - In `packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs`, add the node key `highlighted` after `clickable`. `NODE_FIELDS`
     becomes `[NodeFieldSpec; 15]`. Its help states: a closed bool, true on the one row an open list highlights,
     written only when true.
   - In `packages/escher-driver/src/json/snapshot.rs`, write `highlighted: true` only when true, after `clickable`.
     Map `Reading::Highlighted` to its `NODE_FIELDS` index, and shift `bounds` and `differs`.
   - Update `packages/escher-driver/src/schema_tests.rs` (the fifteen names, the count 15) and
     `packages/escher-driver/src/json_tests.rs` (`Reading::ALL.len()` 13, the full node's keys, a node holding
     `highlighted`).
   - `describe.rs` and the MCP listing read the table and need no edit.

8. **F5 — Cells.** In `examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/cells.rs`, give each data cell
   `aria_selected: is_current.then_some("true")`. The current cell carries `aria-selected="true"`; every other cell
   carries no attribute. No element, class, key, id, style or order moves (layouts S1).

9. **The checks.** Every check runs in both layout modes, pins measured literals and asserts its fixture's condition
   first (arch S2, tests S1, S5):
   - `tests/blitz-tests/tests/select_popup.rs`
     - `the_keys_move_the_highlight_over_enabled_rows_and_choose_nothing`: its assertion «a move marks nothing»
       (`:270`) becomes «a move marks the set», drained per row. A move to the row already highlighted (an `End` at
       the end) still marks nothing.
     - Append after the existing tests: a list whose select is 13px with one option at `font-size: 32px` and a group
       header. Its rows read one height of at least that option's laid-out line height (the literal measured), and
       placement stays finite.
     - Append a tree test: while open, the select's node names the highlighted option as its active descendant
       through keys and a pointer move; none when closed; the tree's focus stays on the select.
   - `tests/blitz-tests/tests/select_popup_painted.rs` — append:
     - The shared pair: a `multiple` select's chosen row, read through `text_contrast` at the default sheet, has the
       same text and background as `SelectListView::HIGHLIGHT_TEXT` and `HIGHLIGHT_BACKGROUND` (each as a measured
       literal channel triple).
     - `highlight_contrast` answers the painted 12.56 on the highlighted row (a measured literal, ±0.2) and `None` on
       a plain row and with the list closed.
     - The 32px option's glyph pixels lie wholly inside its row's rect in a shot.
   - `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_lint.rs` — append a fixture: a select whose plain options read below 4.5 (a
     measured pair), its list open on one option. The lint names a `contrast` finding on the plain rows and none on
     the highlighted row.
   - `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_popup.rs` — append: a driver `press` of an arrow key in an open list returns a
     diff naming the old and new rows with `differs` holding `highlighted`. The snapshot text holds one
     `highlighted` token on the new row, and none once the list closes.
   - `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_cells_served.rs` — append: Cells at boot reads `cell-A0` `selected` and no other
     cell selected; after ArrowRight `cell-B0` reads it and `cell-A0` no longer does; the diff names both with
     `differs: ["selected"]`.
   - `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_cross_os_readings.rs` — re-read Cells' digests on this host and pin them. A
     temporary print is restored by its saved bytes, its sha256 compared before the green reading (testing.md,
     2026-11-19). The other six tasks' rows are unchanged: no other served task opens a list or is a Cells screen.
     Their re-reading is the check itself.

10. **The capability statement.** In `docs/capabilities.md`:
    - «fourteen node keys» → «fifteen», naming `highlighted`.
    - The limit «The highlight is unread» (`:358-360`) is replaced by what is now read: the tree's active
      descendant, the snapshot's `highlighted`, the lint's painted pair. Its pin becomes `select_popup` /
      `select_popup_painted` / `stand_act_popup` / `stand_lint`.
    - In «The list's thumb and one row height» (`:361-363`), the clip clause becomes «one height, the tallest row's».
    - «A single select's `size` is unread» stays, with the founder's word that it is owed by a route entry of its own.
    - Cells: state that the current cell reads `selected`.
    - `## Where each claim is proven` is updated by hand for the new checks (testing.md §File and naming conventions).
- none
- `packages/blitz-test-harness/src/contrast.rs` — `Harness::highlight_contrast` (step 1)
- `packages/escher-driver/src/lint.rs` — the highlighted row read as painted (step 2)
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs` — the tallest row's height; a highlight move marks the set (steps 3, 5)
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs` — the pointer's highlight move marks the set (step 5)
- `packages/blitz-dom/src/accessibility.rs` — the single select's active descendant (step 4)
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot.rs` — `NodeState.highlighted` (step 6)
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot_text.rs` — the `highlighted` token (step 6)
- `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot_diff.rs` — `Reading::Highlighted` (step 6)
- `packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs` — the fifteenth node key (step 7)
- `packages/escher-driver/src/schema_tests.rs` — the node-key pin (step 7)
- `packages/escher-driver/src/json/snapshot.rs` — the written field and its index (step 7)
- `packages/escher-driver/src/json_tests.rs` — the reading count and keys (step 7)
- `examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/cells.rs` — `aria-selected` on the current cell (step 8)
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/select_popup.rs` — row height, active descendant, marks (step 9)
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/select_popup_painted.rs` — the shared pair, the reader, the unclipped glyph (step 9)
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_lint.rs` — the highlighted row read as painted (step 9)
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_popup.rs` — `highlighted` in a press's diff (step 9)
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_cells_served.rs` — the current cell selected (step 9)
- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_cross_os_readings.rs` — Cells' digests re-read (step 9)
- `docs/capabilities.md` — keys, limits, Cells (step 10)
The gates:
- the unit tests of the four touched library crates;

- the blitz-tests targets the steps write, plus their companions: the snapshot's text, parts and diff checks, the
  keyboard walk, the tree-state checks, contrast, select interaction, the MCP listing and the replay;
- seven_guis' process checks;
- the capability-statement pin;
- the a11y leg (`stand_keyboard`, `select_interaction` and `accessibility_active_descendant_unread` are in it);

- the pre-push gate (`fast`); the `doc` leg, because public doc comments change (`NodeState`, `Reading`,
  `Harness::highlight_contrast`, the `NODE_FIELDS` help) and `fast` runs no rustdoc;
- `stand-repeat`.

No boot-path touchpoint changes a binary's start; `host_log`, `mcp_log`, `mcp_server` and `cli_commands` drive both
roles and stand in for the smoke. There is no live leg; the cold-agent pipe is not run. Its `list_opens` counter reads
rows whose `differs` is exactly `bounds`. An opening still moves every other row by `bounds` alone, so it is
unaffected, and its contract tests run in `fast`'s CI-scripts step.

Each new check is controlled red-before-green (tests S4). After the steps are green, /implement makes five one-shot
`gate.py control` runs, never entries:

- **The painted read removed.** In `lint.rs`, delete the `highlight_contrast` call so only `text_contrast` is read.
  Fired on the blitz-tests entry, case: step 9's `stand_lint` test.

- **The row height from the select again.** In `document.rs` `measure_select_list`, return the select's own line
  height alone. Fired on the blitz-tests entry, case: step 9's `select_popup` row-height test.

- **No active descendant.** In `accessibility.rs`, delete the `set_active_descendant` call. Fired on the blitz-tests
  entry, case: step 9's `select_popup` tree test.

- **A move marks nothing.** In `document.rs` `move_select_list_current`, delete the `changed_nodes` insert. Fired on
  the blitz-tests entry, case `the_keys_move_the_highlight_over_enabled_rows_and_choose_nothing`.

- **Cells states nothing.** In `cells.rs`, delete the `aria_selected` line. Fired on the blitz-tests entry, case:
  step 9's `stand_cells_served` test.

Each control names the edit's text and the case by its test name, with `--no-fail-fast` reaching it
(gate-contract.md §Control).

An acceptance reads CI: the windows and macOS legs of `matrix_test` hold the re-read Cells digests. So the
operator's hygiene, push and CI entries stand. The diff is OS-sensitive only through those digests; no `cfg` site is
added or changed.

body:
- (a11y) The lint reads an open list's highlighted row at its painted 12.56:1 and no contrast finding on it, while
  plain rows below 4.5 still read findings; the shared pair is pinned to the default sheet's chosen row (a11y-plan ·
  decision/lint-contrast-single-formula — through `contrast_ratio`, no second formula).

- (a11y) No row of an open list is shorter than its own laid-out line: a 32px option in a 13px select is painted whole
  inside its row (a11y-plan · decision/select-list-rows-one-height, its direction changed).

- (a11y) While a single select's list is open, the tree names the highlighted option as the select's active
  descendant, the tree's focus stays on the select, and `stand_keyboard`'s list walks stay green (a11y-plan ·
  decision/focus-stays-on-select-with-list-open).

- (driver) The snapshot carries `highlighted` on the one highlighted row only, its text a bare token and its JSON
  `true`, written only when true. A `press` in an open list returns a diff whose changed rows' `differs` hold
  `highlighted`. `NODE_FIELDS` reads fifteen and `Reading::ALL` thirteen. The committed Counter checks replay
  byte-equal (security-plan · decision/snapshot-state-readings; architecture · contract/snapshot-node-keys/expanded).

- (stand) Cells' current cell reads `selected`, and only it; an arrow moves the reading. Cells' Tab walk and ratios
  are unchanged (`stand_keyboard`, `stand_contrast` green).

- (tests) The cross-OS readings hold on linux, windows and macOS (CI `matrix_test`), and `stand-repeat` reads
  `3 of 3 rounds green`.

- (tests) `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh fast` and the `doc` and `a11y` legs read green; CI on the pushed HEAD reads
  `verdict: green`.

- Rulings: inputs#I2 (the founder, F1 A · F2 A · F3 A · F4 C · F5 A) · inputs#I3 (the operator, the harness reader) ·
  inputs#I1 (the relay directive).

- Rows:
  - a11y-plan · decision/highlighted-row-contrast-unread · decision/select-list-rows-one-height ·
    contract/snapshot/open-list-highlighted-row · decision/changed-set-marks · decision/active-descendant-unread ·
    decision/lint-contrast-single-formula · decision/snapshot-reads-the-tree ·
    decision/focus-stays-on-select-with-list-open
  - design-system · decision/select-list-colours-engine-constants · decision/select-chosen-row-chromium-pair
  - architecture · contract/snapshot/node-state · contract/snapshot-diff/reading ·
    contract/snapshot-node-keys/expanded · contract/snapshot-text/state-tokens · decision/select-list-crossing
  - security-plan · decision/boundary-widening-rule · decision/snapshot-state-readings · decision/select-list-crossing
  - layout-templates · decision/stand-a11y-by-attributes-alone · contract/stand-element-ids/cell-column-row
  - test-plan · decision/contrast-reader-reads-only · contract/harness-contrast/text-contrast
- Research files: as `doc:2026-11-20-select-list-and-selection-debts/research` lists them.
- Per-row list heights (F2 B): rejected by the founder (inputs#I2); `Geometry` keeps one row height.
- Moving the tree's focus to the highlighted row (F3 C): rejected; tree focus stays on the select.
- A single select's `size` as a list box (F4 A): not in this chunk (F4 C); no sheet, hint or key change for it.
- `aria-selected="false"` on every other cell (F5 C), or grid roles (F5 B): rejected; the current cell alone.
- Widening `text_contrast` or adding `color` to escher-driver: rejected by the operator (inputs#I3).
- Reading `aria-activedescendant` from a page: never; the engine writes the active descendant itself.
- Order: steps 1–2, 3, 4–7, 8, then 9–10. Step 6 before step 7, because the driver's JSON reads `NodeState`.

- `has_changes` trap: a fresh harness document holds a non-empty set. A check reading «this step marked» drains first
  (a11y-plan · decision/harness-settle-leaves-changed-set).

- The committed Counter checks (`tests/blitz-tests/checks/counter-*.json`) hold no open list and no Cells screen. A
  key written only when true leaves their answers byte-equal (seven_guis `recording` re-reads them).

- The Cells snapshot measured 53,890 bytes in 6 parts at HEAD 3ff72e8da (research §Measurements). F5 adds one
  ` selected` token, a forecast of +9 bytes: record what the re-read measures. The part count is not pinned by
  any check (`git grep -n "parts" tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_cells_served.rs` re-read at implement).

- Expected amendments (wrap):
  - a11y-plan — decision/highlighted-row-contrast-unread retired, the lint reading the painted pair in its place.
  - a11y-plan — decision/select-list-rows-one-height: the tallest row's height, no clip.
  - a11y-plan — contract/snapshot/open-list-highlighted-row and contract/snapshot/select-list-rows: the highlight read
    in the tree and the snapshot.
  - a11y-plan — decision/changed-set-marks: a highlight move marks.
  - design-system — contract/select-accessibility/highlighted-row and decision/select-list-colours-engine-constants:
    the pin to the chosen row.
  - architecture — contract/snapshot/node-state (nine fields) · contract/snapshot-diff/reading (thirteen) ·
    contract/snapshot-node-keys/expanded (fifteen keys) · contract/snapshot-text/state-tokens (`highlighted`) ·
    decision/select-list-crossing.
  - security-plan — decision/select-list-crossing and decision/snapshot-state-readings: a fourth closed state, the
    highlight. Under the playbook's pattern `rul-izni57qv` (Boundary widening) this is a closed bool inside a
    ratified carrier (the 2026-10-10 rule). It is answered by the founder's own F3 A, relayed by the overseer
    (inputs#I2).

**Chunk:** the select list's highlight contrast, larger font, highlight reading, single size, and Cells' selected cell — each fixed or kept by the founder's fork
**Date:** 2026-11-20
**Run:** 2026-11-20T16-06-30-implement

- **Files:** `packages/blitz-test-harness/src/contrast.rs` · `packages/escher-driver/src/lint.rs` · `packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs` · `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs` · `packages/blitz-dom/src/accessibility.rs` · `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot.rs` · `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot_text.rs` · `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot_diff.rs` · `packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs` · `packages/escher-driver/src/schema_tests.rs` · `packages/escher-driver/src/json/snapshot.rs` · `packages/escher-driver/src/json/diff.rs` · `packages/escher-driver/src/json_tests.rs` · `packages/escher-driver/src/describe.rs` · `examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/cells.rs` · `tests/blitz-tests/tests/select_popup.rs` · `tests/blitz-tests/tests/select_popup_painted.rs` · `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_lint.rs` · `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_popup.rs` · `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_cells_served.rs` · `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_cross_os_readings.rs` · `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_diff.rs` · `docs/capabilities.md` (23; `gate.py scope`: changed 23 · listed 20 · recorded 3)

- **Symbols / APIs:**
  - NEW `blitz_test_harness::Harness::highlight_contrast(&self, NodeId) -> Option<TextContrast>` (public, read-only: no mutation, pump, settle or time move; prints and logs nothing; `packages/blitz-test-harness/src/contrast.rs` 92-122, new-text listing). It answers only for the highlighted row of the open list, read through `BaseDocument::select_list_view()`: text `SelectListView::HIGHLIGHT_TEXT` on `HIGHLIGHT_BACKGROUND`, through the one `contrast_ratio`, with font size and weight from the option's computed font. `text_contrast` is unchanged. Its one non-test caller is the lint.
  - CHANGED `escher_driver` lint `contrast()` (private): reads `harness.highlight_contrast(element)` first and `harness.text_contrast(element)` where it answers `None`. The finding's shape, order and written form are unchanged.
  - CHANGED `BaseDocument::measure_select_list` (private): the row height is the largest `layout.height()` among the rows' own layouts (a header at weight 700), with the select's own one-line height as the floor, divided by the scale, plus `2 × ROW_PADDING_Y`. `SelectList.row_height` stays one value.
  - CHANGED `BaseDocument::move_select_list_current` (crate-private; its caller `press_open_list_key`) and `events::pointer::hover_list_row` (private): a highlight move to another row inserts the list's select into `changed_nodes`. A move to the same row and a wheel move inside the list mark nothing.
  - CHANGED accessibility builder, single-select arm: while the list stands open with `current` `Some(option)`, `builder.set_active_descendant(option)`. Nothing is read from a page's `aria-activedescendant`; the tree's focus stays on the select.
  - NEW field `dioxus_native_dom::NodeState.highlighted: bool` (public), read from the tree as "a tree node names this node as its active descendant". NEW variant `dioxus_native_dom::Reading::Highlighted` (public), before `Bounds`; `Reading::ALL` 12 → 13. Snapshot text token ` highlighted` after ` clickable`, written only when true.
  - CHANGED `escher_driver::NODE_FIELDS` (public): `[NodeFieldSpec; 14]` → `[NodeFieldSpec; 15]`, `highlighted` after `clickable`. The help strings for snapshot `text` and acting `changed` name `highlighted`. The JSON node writes `"highlighted":true` only when true. `reading_word` maps `Highlighted` → 12, `Bounds` → 13.
  - Stand: Cells' data cell `aria_selected: is_current.then_some("true")` (`examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/cells.rs` 470).
- **Crates / modules:** changed — blitz-dom, blitz-test-harness, dioxus-native-dom, escher-driver, seven_guis (stand), blitz-tests (checks). None added or removed.
- **Dependencies:** none (`Cargo.toml` / `Cargo.lock` untouched).

- **Schema / config:** the driver's node-key schema gains `highlighted`, a closed bool written only when true, inside the ratified snapshot and diff carriers (the snapshot text, the diff's `changed` / `added` nodes, `help`'s `node_keys` with 15 entries, MCP tool descriptions read from the table). The diff's `differs` can name `highlighted`. No new carrier, verb, argument, exit, cause, session error, log field or span. The committed Counter checks are byte-equal (seven_guis `recording` and `stand_replay` green).
- **Spec-master edits:** none.
- **Retired:** the limit «The highlight is unread» in `docs/capabilities.md` (replaced by «How the highlight is read»), and the clause «a row with a larger authored font clips».

- **Counts / qualifiers moved:**
  - node keys 14 → 15 (`docs/capabilities.md` «fifteen node keys»; `describe.rs`'s `counts`; `schema_tests.rs`'s `NODE_FIELDS.len()`)
  - `Reading::ALL` 12 → 13 (`json_tests.rs`, `snapshot_diff.rs` tests)
  - `NodeState` fields 8 → 9
  - `select_popup` 25 → 27 tests · `select_popup_painted` 6 → 9 · `stand_act_popup` 12 → 13 · `stand_lint` 9 → 10 · `stand_cells_served` 5 → 6 (each read from `test result:` in `2.4.log` / the hand runs)
  - Cells' cross-OS digests: two re-pinned values (part 0/1 at boot and after the step)
  - a11y.md's «a highlight or a wheel move inside it marks nothing» now reads false for a highlight move
- **Dev-tool versions:** none.
- **Harness / gate surface:** `Harness::highlight_contrast` (blitz-test-harness's public API; test-plan contract/harness-contrast). No agent-run, CI or status shape changed.

- **Cross-project / external claims:**
  - inputs#I1 · relay · message: operator (`/andromeda-phase` invocation) — the founder answers by relay in one forks file.
  - inputs#I2 · relay · `../additional/escher-overseer/relays/select-list-debts-founder-2026-11-20.md` — the founder's F1 A · F2 A · F3 A · F4 C · F5 A, ratifying F2's and F3's engine changes.

    | # | Proposal | Owner |
    |---|---|---|
    | 1 | A new route entry for a single select's `size` rendered as a list box (HTML's rendering, `size` × 1.2em, keys moving the choice, no popup). Proposed title «Single select sized as a list box», placed in Epoch 2 «Debts of 0.1.0–0.3.0» after «Engine debts», on the founder's F4 C (inputs#I2). | the wrap's route-resolve |
    | 2 | The residual `res-ysz67imk` re-targeted from v040-04 to that new entry, with the founder's reason. | the wrap |
- **Reverted / negative API facts:** none.

- **Spec claims disproved by measurement:**
  - The plan (step 9, `stand_cells_served`) forecast the arrow's diff naming both cells with `differs: ["selected"]`. Measured: `[selected, bounds]`, since the arrow brings the current cell into view. Pinned as measured.
  - The plan's forecast of +9 bytes and an unchanged part count for Cells: the part count stays 6 (`stand_cells_served`'s `PARTS = 6` green). The byte count was not re-measured.

title: 2026-11-20-select-list-and-selection-debts — 3. Test Harness Contract: 1 row(s)
body:
## 2026-11-20-select-list-and-selection-debts — 3. Test Harness Contract: 1 row(s)
**Section:** 3. Test Harness Contract
**Change:** ~ decision/one-contrast-formula · rule: was «Session lint's contrast reads the same as the harness's text_contrast, with no second formula.»; now «Session lint's contrast reads through the harness's contrast readers, with no second formula.»
**Why:** decision/one-contrast-formula: The row's «reads the same as the harness's text_contrast» is false since the lint reads the highlight reader too; fit read the call order not_master, so the row keeps its one-formula rule without naming one reader.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-11-20T17-45-40-wrap/

- **Contrast harness:** built since 2026-10-13-stand-contrast-harness — `Harness::text_contrast` (blitz-test-harness, read-only) reads an element's text/background pair and font metrics from computed styles as a `TextContrast` (`ratio` by `contrast_ratio`, the WCAG 2.x formula restating blitz-paint's Chrome-matching helper; `required_ratio` 3.0 for large text, else 4.5); `stand_contrast` states three tables, read by one shared reader and asserted row for row in both layout modes — the 17 control rows beside a painted-pixel witness (pass 13, fail 0, exempt-inactive 3, no-text 1: since 2026-10-14-stand-a11y-assertions the stand's accent is one step darker, the operator's F5, a stand change and no engine change, so the four accent controls read `#ffffff` on `#3a5ce5` at 5.47 where `#4a6cf7` read 4.39 and failed), 14 `TEXT_ROWS` (the CRUD list rows and the text outside the controls, all pass) and 20 `STATE_ROWS` (the colour states reached by input, hover and active included: pass 19, exempt 1) — so SC 1.4.3 is met on every measured non-exempt stand row; it runs in the workspace `test` leg, per package and, since 2026-10-14-stand-a11y-assertions, in the `a11y` leg. Since 2026-10-19-visual-lint its first non-test caller is escher-driver's visual lint (`Session::lint` in process and the `lint` verb on every carrier, recorded), whose `contrast` reading reports a node below `required_ratio()` and keeps the same exempt rule (`enabled == Some(false)`), with no second formula or threshold. The default sheet holds an engine-default chosen-row pair for a `multiple` select's rows, `#000000` on `#c8c8c8`, Chromium's inactive selected pair, hardcoded by design as the engine holds no tokens, 12.56:1 measured by `select_interaction` in both layout modes. An open select list's colours are engine constants on `SelectListView`, in no sheet — `HIGHLIGHT_TEXT` `#000000`, `HIGHLIGHT_BACKGROUND` `#c8c8c8`, `DISABLED_TEXT` `#6d6d6d`, `BORDER` `#999999` — and `select_popup_painted` reads the highlight and a disabled row as painted against those constants and measures the plain pair at the default sheet and at the stand, in both layout modes, so SC 1.4.3 is asserted on the list in the harness; the lint reads an open list's highlighted row at its painted pair through the harness's highlight reader first, the text contrast where it answers nothing, with the one formula, required ratio and exempt rule, and a blended text's pair is unread by the lint (`Harness::text_contrast` reading `None` past an element on its walk with opacity below 1, a non-empty filter, a background-image layer or a `mix-blend-mode` other than `normal`, pinned by `a_blended_ancestor_reads_none_and_an_unblended_one_its_pair`, no stand row moving) and a closed select's own pair is unread.

- Roles: `role` attribute → HTML-AAM mapping → `Role::Unknown`; landmarks, lists, tables, form inputs by `type`, links only with `href`; an `img` whose `alt` is the empty string decorative, reading the generic container role and not image (ratified as upstream's behaviour); a single select's `ComboBox` writes `expanded` from its list's open state, reading no `aria-expanded`, an author's `open` or `aria-expanded` on it steering nothing and `:open` not matching it; the tree's focus stays on the select and its chosen option reads `selected`; while its list is open the tree names the highlighted option as the select's active descendant and the snapshot, taking `highlighted` from the tree, reads that row alone highlighted, and the snapshot holds no `expanded` key, and what an assistive technology reads of the list is not measured; a `multiple` select's `ListBox` writes `set_multiselectable`, and an `optgroup` reads `Role::Group`, its non-empty `label` attribute its name, named in the tree and painted as a header of an open list, heavier than a row by weight on every build, a header choosing nothing — what an assistive technology reads of them is not measured.

- Platform: accesskit_xplat adapters (windows, macos, unix, android, null); ActionRequested and AccessibilityDeactivated are unhandled TODOs; the tree is built on InitialTreeRequested and pushed again in a redraw, after style resolve, only when the document's changed set, taken and cleared by that redraw, was non-empty, a poll pushing no tree — a focus move, a checked change, a rewritten name, a text control's input, a select's changed choice, a single select's list opening or closing and other mutations mark it, a page scroll or a move that closes a list marking its select through `reconcile_select_list` at the next resolve and a wheel elsewhere through `close_select_list`, and its highlight moving to another row marking it too, while a wheel move inside a list marks nothing and a pointer move alone does not — through `Document::accessibility_tree` (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-07; before 2026-10-07 the poll-time refresh never ran; no windowed witness on the dev host — still owed at the platform adapter, the stand building no adapter, kept so on the founder's F1 (2026-10-14), and owned by residual `res-llkgqygv` (re-carried at 0.3.0, target: next), an active assistive technology this version does not reach; since 2026-10-14-stand-a11y-assertions both halves are proven headlessly on the stand in both layout modes: on Counter, after a drained changed set, each Tab of the whole `tab_order` and an Enter on `counter-increment` leave `has_changes()` true, and the tree read through `&dyn Document` reads the new focus stop and `counter-value`'s new name). A harness settle neither reads nor drains that changed set, and the set is non-empty on a freshly booted harness document — a check reading the flag as "this step changed something" drains first. Names come from text children, a trimmed-non-empty `aria-label` and `<label>` association (`for`-target, else first nested labelable element — a `button`, an `input` whose `type` is not `hidden`, a `meter`, `output`, `progress`, `select` or `textarea`; a hidden input is named by no label); since 2026-10-17-upstream-sync-engine-debts an `aria-labelledby` whose targets hold text outranks both (accname 2B) — its loop runs after the `<label>` → input loop, clears `labelled_by` and pushes the referenced nodes, the `aria-label` staying the fallback when the targets hold none — and that text reaches the snapshot `name`. The seven_guis stand names no `accessibility` feature in its own manifest — dioxus-native-dom's reaches it through escher-driver, so both its binaries compile the accessibility modules — and builds no platform adapter (`accesskit_xplat` and `accesskit_winit` in neither graph), so the stand binary gives no assistive technology a tree; re-read at 2026-10-10-mcp-surface, when escher-driver took `serde_json` as a fourth dependency (one lock line, no package), no platform adapter joins the stand graph.

- State = ARIA state attributes read by value on every element — a select's option excepted, its `selected` its chosen state (`select::is_chosen`), true or false, with no `aria-selected` read, and its non-empty `label` attribute its `label` where it has no `aria-label` —, the toggle by role (trimmed, lower-case, exact): `aria-selected` `true`/`false` → `selected`; `aria-pressed` `true`/`false`/`mixed` → `toggled` on every role but the five checkable ones; `aria-invalid` `true`/`grammar`/`spelling` → `invalid`, absent, empty or `false` → nothing, any other value → `Invalid::True`. `aria-checked` `true`/`false`/`mixed` → `toggled` on a `CheckBox` · `Switch` · `RadioButton` · `MenuItemCheckBox` · `MenuItemRadio` role alone (`role="switch"` mapping to `Switch`), a native `input` of type `checkbox` or `radio` reading neither attribute — the toggle read per role ratified by the founder (2026-10-18), `accessibility_states`' fourth test its pin; each attribute is read once, and the one other write of `toggled` is a native checkbox's or radio's own checked state on a checkable role — `Toggled::True` or `False` from `checkbox_input_checked()`; under any other role it writes nothing, so `pressed` never begins to read on it, `accessibility_states`' `a_click_and_a_space_move_a_native_control_in_the_tree` its pin, what an assistive technology reads of it not measured. A Dioxus `bool` attribute arrives as the text `"false"`, so state the literal texts `"true"` and `"false"`: a presence read would read every control pressed. Since 2026-10-17-upstream-sync-engine-debts the builder also holds upstream's `aria-describedby` (→ `described_by`), `aria-description` (→ description), `aria-expanded` (a boolean, on every element but a single select, which reads none and writes `expanded` from its list's open state), `aria-disabled` (`true` → `set_disabled`) and `aria-level` (read as its number less one, headings keeping their default levels) reads beside the three, as upstream wrote them; upstream's own `parse::<bool>` `aria-selected` and unfiltered `aria-label` reads were dropped in the merge, so there is still one read per attribute — keep it so. The snapshot takes the three, and its `highlighted` reading, from the tree node, never from the element, its `checked` is a native checkbox's or radio's state, else, on a checkable role, the node's `toggled` (`Mixed` reading false; ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18), reads no description, and reads `enabled` from the `disabled` attribute, so `aria-disabled` moves no snapshot reading; since 2026-10-12-self-description the driver's served node-key help (`help`) states the boolean model's two limits (a mixed toggle reads `pressed` false, a grammar or spelling error reads `invalid` true). Ratified by the founder (2026-10-10); what an assistive technology reads of them is unmeasured — the windowed witness, at an active assistive technology, which this version does not reach, owned by residual `res-llkgqygv` (re-carried at 0.3.0, target: next) on the founder's F1 (2026-10-14), the headless half — the tree the shell hands the adapter — proven on the stand since 2026-10-14-stand-a11y-assertions.

- Text nodes become `TextRun` nodes and label their parent; an `aria-label` non-empty after trimming sets `label`; a `<label>` is pushed onto its bound labelable element's `labelled_by` (`for`-target, else first nested labelable element — a `button`, an `input` whose `type` is not `hidden`, a `meter`, `output`, `progress`, `select` or `textarea`; a hidden input is named by no label) after the whole tree is built; since 2026-10-17-upstream-sync-engine-debts an `aria-labelledby` loop runs after that `<label>` → input loop, clears `labelled_by`, pushes the referenced nodes and sets their computed text as the `label`, so it outranks a `<label>` and an `aria-label` (accname 2B) — an id naming no built node ignored, hidden targets read for the label, the `aria-label` the fallback when the targets hold no text. A `select` (role `ComboBox`, `ListBox` for `multiple`) keeps its `option` children, and those under an `optgroup`, in the tree as `ListBoxOption` nodes, under `display: none` too, each `selected` true or false from its chosen state and named by its non-empty `label` attribute, else its text; the snapshot reads a `select`'s `value` as `BaseDocument::select_value` (the chosen option's value, for a `multiple` select its first chosen option's in tree order, nothing with none chosen) and a closed select's options under it, each with its select's client rect as its `bounds` — which the driver's visual lint leaves out of its overlap reading in every document (`overlaps` skipping such an entry on either side, `Entry.in_select_box` true for an option of a closed select, read through `closed_select_of` and never the role, and for an open list's row or group, read through `select_list_bounds`, so CRUD's `role="option"` rows are not read as a select's), the stand's flight booker at boot reading no `overlap`, `stand_lint` reading `[0, 0, 0, 0]`. A select whose list is open is no closed select, `closed_select_of` answering `None` for it, and the snapshot's builder reads `select_list_bounds(node)` before the client rect, so an open row's `bounds` is its painted row's in the snapshot and the diff, `differs` naming `bounds`. A single select's tree node takes `expanded` from a closed bool of engine state, reading no `aria-expanded`, its focus staying on the select while the list is open and its chosen option reading `selected`; an author's `open` or `aria-expanded` on it steers nothing and `:open` does not match it; the tree names the highlighted option as the select's active descendant, its focus staying on the select, and the snapshot reads that row alone `highlighted`, and `NodeState` holds no `expanded` field (`NODE_FIELDS` fourteen), so a list's open state reaches the tree and not the snapshot; what an assistive technology reads of an open list is not measured and the windowed list is read and not run. **What breaks:** reading `has_changes()` / `take_changed_nodes()` as "what an agent sees changed". The set is engine-touched: an attribute re-written to itself marks and changes no reading, a further character in a masked password marks and changes no reading, and bounds-only movement (a re-wrap, a scroll with no select list standing) changes a reading and marks nothing, while a select list's opening or closing, a page scroll or a move of the select's box that closes it included, marks its select, and a highlight move to another row, by key or pointer, marks its select, while a move to the same row or a wheel move inside the list marks nothing. It holds `NodeId`s of text nodes too, and a drained id may name a dropped node.
**How to avoid:** take what changed from `Snapshot::diff` over two snapshots; read a drained id through `get_node`; drain before a step you want to observe (after boot the set holds the initial build).

- `Harness::settle() -> Result<Settled, NotSettled>` — runs every pass that is due, then says whether anything is outstanding: `Settled { passes, animating }`, or `NotSettled { busy }` with `Busy` one of `Render` · `Layout` · `Loads` — a load in flight after a quiet pass reported at once as `Loads`, and after `SETTLE_PASS_LIMIT` = 64 passes with none quiet the class read off the last pass (`Render` when its poll answered `true`, else `Loads` when a load finished in it, else `Layout`). The outcome names a class only — no node, id, name, URL or value. Since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot `Harness::screenshot(&mut self) -> Result<Raster, ScreenshotError>` and `screenshot_rect(&mut self, PixelRect) -> Result<Raster, ScreenshotError>` resolve at the harness's own time (no tick, no pump), paint the viewport at its scale and device size into `VelloCpuImageRenderer` and composite over opaque white (premultiplied source-over); a rectangle is clipped to the viewport and an empty one is `EmptyRect`; a document whose `can_paint_text` reads false is `FontsUnavailable` with nothing painted; no path prints, panics or logs. Since 2026-10-13-stand-contrast-harness `Harness::text_contrast(&self, NodeId) -> Option<TextContrast>` reads and changes nothing (no `doc.mutate()`, input, pump or settle; every node by `get_node`): the text-bearing element — the node itself when it is a text input, else the parent element of the first text node under it holding a character other than whitespace — gives its computed `color`, `font-size` and `font-weight`, over a background composited source-over from each element's `background-color` up through its ancestors to the first opaque one, else onto the canvas (the root element's background, else `body`'s) over opaque white; it reads `None` for no such text, for an element on the walk without primary styles, and for one up to the first opaque whose `opacity` is below 1, whose `filter` list is not empty, whose `background-image` holds a layer other than `none` or whose `mix-blend-mode` is other than `normal`; `TextContrast { text, background, ratio, font_size_px, font_weight }` has `is_large_text()` (at least 24 px, or 14 pt at weight 700 or more) and `required_ratio()` (3.0 for large text, else 4.5); `contrast_ratio(a, b) -> f32` is the WCAG 2.x ratio `(L1 + 0.05) / (L2 + 0.05)` over the `color` crate's relative luminance, alpha ignored; it opens no span and prints or logs nothing. `Harness::highlight_contrast(&self, NodeId) -> Option<TextContrast>`, a public read-only reader, answers only for the highlighted row of an open select list, with the list's highlight text and background through the one `contrast_ratio` and the option's own font size and weight, and `None` for any other node; like `text_contrast` it changes nothing (no mutation, input, pump or settle).
